name: One Thing Changed
why_it_works: Spot-the-difference is a tiny puzzle with a clear right answer, so people rewatch until they find it, and every rewatch counts. Finding it feels smart, which makes people want to prove it in the comments before the reveal shows up.

hook.pattern: Show a detailed scene and say one thing will change. Give them a time limit.
examples: Watch close. One thing changes. Five seconds to find it.
Most people miss what changes. Do you?
Same photo twice. One detail is different. Go.

variables.name: scene
variables.description: The busy, detail-rich space or object
variables.example: the barber station at chair three

variables.name: changed_detail
variables.description: The one small detail swapped in the second image, a short sentence starting with a capital, 8 words or fewer
variables.example: The comb in the jar turned gold

variables.name: reward
variables.description: What people who get it right receive, 5 words or fewer

beats.purpose: hook: set the challenge on image A

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 wide, sharp, evenly lit photo of {{scene}} at {{brand}}, lots of small objects and texture in frame, no people, deep focus front to back
The exact same vertical 9:16 photo of {{scene}} at {{brand}}, identical framing and light, with one change only: {{changed_detail}}
Slow push-in from the full image B of {{scene}} down to {{changed_detail}}, a thin circle drawing around it, vertical 9:16

cta: Comment the change before the reveal, then show your comment at {{brand}} for {{reward}}.

craft.notes: Generate image B by editing image A, not by prompting a new image, or a dozen things will drift and the game breaks. The change should be findable in about four seconds: obvious once seen, invisible at first glance.

do_not: Let anything besides the one detail shift between images; people will call it rigged
Make the change so tiny it needs a zoom; frustration kills the replay
Put the answer in the caption
compliance: Real estate: only alter removable staging props, never walls, fixtures, views or anything that changes how the property is represented
Real estate: show the brokerage name and follow your state's advertising rules on every listing post
Rewards: state any limits (one per person, end date) and that no purchase is needed to play
